articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring substantially improved long-horizon reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a unified architecture that merges previously separate models. Benchmarks show significant gains on PhD-level science QA and complex multi-step coding tasks, with latency improvements attributed to a new mixture-of-experts inference pipeline.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Ultra Achieves State-of-the-Art on Agentic Coding Benchmarks
articles.summary: DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Ultra, which tops SWE-Bench Verified and a new internal multi-repo refactoring benchmark with autonomous tool use. The model demonstrates the ability to plan and execute complex software engineering workflows across multiple files and repositories with minimal human intervention, signaling a shift toward AI-native software development pipelines.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Humanoid Workers at BMW Facility
articles.summary: Figure AI announced the first scaled commercial deployment of its Figure 02 humanoid robots at BMW's Spartanburg plant, with over 50 units performing parts inspection, kitting, and light assembly tasks across multiple shifts. The deployment uses on-device vision-language models for task understanding, marking a milestone in humanoid robotics moving from demos to production floor operations.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Demonstrates Autonomous Household Task Completion in Unseen Environments
articles.summary: Tesla showcased its Optimus Gen 3 humanoid performing a sequence of household chores—including laundry folding, dish loading, and surface cleaning—in homes it had never been trained in, using a foundation world model for spatial reasoning and manipulation. The demo highlights advances in sim-to-real transfer and few-shot generalization for domestic robotics applications.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces 'Constitutional Classifiers' Framework to Mitigate Jailbreaks at Scale
articles.summary: Anthropic published a technical report on its constitutional classifiers system, a layered defense architecture that reduced successful jailbreak rates on Claude to under 2% on adversarial red-team evaluations. The approach uses lightweight classifier heads trained on synthetically generated attack vectors, providing a meaningful advance in production-grade LLM safety without significant latency penalties.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm GAA Process Node for Next-Gen AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed the start of volume production on its N1.4 process using second-generation gate-all-around transistors, with initial capacity allocated to Nvidia's next-generation Blackwell Ultra AI accelerator dies. The node delivers approximately 25% power efficiency improvement over N2, which is critical for data centers facing escalating power constraints from large-scale AI training clusters.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Approval for Expanded BCI Trial Covering Motor and Speech Restoration
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink approval to expand its PRIME clinical trial to include patients with ALS and brainstem stroke, targeting both motor cursor control and speech synthesis via neural decoding. Early trial participants demonstrated real-time speech output at over 120 words per minute with under 5% error rate, a substantial improvement over prior academic BCI benchmarks.

articles.title: Meta Open-Sources Llama 4 Behemoth with 2 Trillion Parameters Under Permissive License
articles.summary: Meta released Llama 4 Behemoth, a 2-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, under a revised open license permitting commercial use without revenue thresholds. The model matches or exceeds proprietary frontier models on key reasoning and multilingual benchmarks, further intensifying the debate about open-weight models' impact on AI safety governance and competitive dynamics in the foundation model market.
